A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RedTeamCUA framework and RTC-BENCH study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including v4's added Appendix H.6.

before.justification: v3 reports original CUA benchmarking results, end-to-end attack evaluations, defense experiments, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds evaluations of two Opus agents and a manual analysis of end-to-end attack outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same hybrid sandbox, automated contextualized injections, benchmark construction, and decoupled initialization. The agent scaffolding, action translation, and existing evaluators are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 864-example benchmark, nine benign goals, 24 adversarial goals, and OwnCloud, Forum, and RocketChat environments. v4 describes the same selected 50-task end-to-end setting; no new task or environmental scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: v4 adds Claude 4.5 Opus | CUA and Claude 4.6 Opus | CUA to the end-to-end comparison. All five agents from v3 Table 2 remain represented in v4 Figure 3 and Table 3; the decoupled-evaluation and defense comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 introduces manual trajectory classification for the end-to-end analysis. The existing step budgets, observation resolution, and task-selection description remain unchanged. The new Opus 4.5 row reports 46 evaluated cases despite the stated 50-task setup, without explaining the discrepancy.

E4.justification: v4 Table 3 and Appendix H.6 add a focused error analysis distinguishing navigation failures, unsuccessful execution, permission and safety checks, ignored injections, termination, and explicit injection detection. v3 provides aggregate end-to-end ASRs and qualitative explanations without this breakdown. Earlier ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The three-run reporting rule and Appendix H.5 analyses of success in one, two, or all three runs are unchanged. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-specific uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The five existing end-to-end ASRs remain 10%, 42%, 50%, 48%, and 60%. v4 adds Opus 4.5 at 83% (38/46) and Opus 4.6 at 50% (25/50), plus outcome counts such as three versus 25 explicit injection detections. These are additional model results; the unequal denominators limit direct comparison. Retained benchmark and appendix scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The threat assumptions and existing security and evaluation definitions remain unchanged. Neither version contains mathematical theorems or proofs, and v4 introduces no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction update the highest-ASR claim from Sonnet 4.5 at 60% to Opus 4.5 at 83%, and highlight persistent vulnerability in Opus 4.6 despite improved defenses. The framework, benchmark, and broad vulnerability contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 interprets Opus 4.6's explicit injection recognition as meaningful defensive progress despite substantial residual risk. This adds a qualification to the existing capability-versus-vulnerability discussion. The stated benchmark, filename, and cost limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H.6 newly documents operational criteria for manual outcome labels, including distinguishing explicit injection detection from simply ignoring an injection. Hardware, API descriptions, execution settings, system prompts, and code-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to the Claude Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.6 system cards for the newly evaluated agents. The comparison with earlier evaluation frameworks and the claimed research gap remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The end-to-end discussion moves from Section 6 into a dedicated Section 7 and is expanded. Section 5.2 becomes 'Decoupled Eval Results,' the abstract and introduction receive focused revisions, and Appendix H.6 is added. Most prose and document organization are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds an end-to-end ASR bar chart as Figure 3 and an outcome-breakdown table as Table 3. Table 2 is shortened and relocated; its Opus 4 and Sonnet 4.5 results appear in the new displays. Existing figures and appendix tables retain their content and design apart from numbering and minor reflow.

improvement.justification: The newer-agent evaluations and manual outcome breakdown make the end-to-end discussion more informative, particularly by distinguishing capability failures from explicit injection detection. The gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies: Table 3 gives Opus 4.5 an unexplained 46-case denominator under a stated 50-task setup, and Sonnet 4.5's outcome counts total 47 rather than 50. These gaps weaken the precision of the added comparisons.
